result:
**I'd give every human being a reliable, built-in "bullshit detector" for their own mind.**

Not superpowers, not world peace handed to us on a platter, not even infinite clean energy (though I'd take that too). Just the reflexive, automatic ability to notice when we're lying to ourselves—about politics, relationships, our own motivations, tribal loyalties, status games, or comforting delusions.

Think about it: most of the worst things we do to each other and ourselves aren't from pure evil. They're from self-deception that scales. Ideologies that justify cruelty, economic systems that pretend externalities don't exist, personal habits we defend with elaborate rationalizations, leaders we follow because admitting we were wrong feels worse than being wrong.

If people could *feel* their own motivated reasoning the way we feel physical pain when touching something hot, a huge amount of unnecessary suffering would become self-correcting. We'd still disagree. We'd still have conflicts of interest. But we'd waste far less time and blood on fairy tales we tell ourselves.

The beautiful part is it wouldn't require changing human nature—it would just remove the bug that makes our nature so consistently sabotage itself. Everything else (better technology, better institutions, better cultures) becomes much easier when the operating system isn't constantly gaslighting itself.

What about you? If you could flip one variable in the human condition, what would you change?
